issues.failure_explanation: Section 3.1 defines B^0 with p-fold boundary knots so that all 0-form splines vanish on the boundary; consequently B^1=(B^1⊗B^0)×(B^0⊗B^1) has vanishing tangential components. The continuous complex introduced in Section 2 is the natural-BC complex H^1→H(curl)→L^2 with H^0≅R and H^2=0, whereas the stated discrete complex has ker(grad)={0} and L^2-cohomology of dimension 1, so the claim of cohomological equivalence is false as written. The same convention makes the numerical claims inconsistent: u=(x(1-x),0) has nonzero tangential component on y=0,1, so u∉T^1_L under the stated definition, and the Maxwell section treats T^1_L as having boundary DoFs to be removed (T^1∩H_0(curl)), i.e. as a space without built-in boundary conditions.

issues.failure_explanation: The truncated function T is obtained by iterated truncation at levels ℓ+1,…,L. A level-ℓ̃ child b of the mother that is nonzero on Q can have zero coefficient in T because all of its level-ℓ' ancestors (ℓ<ℓ'<ℓ̃) had support in Ω_{ℓ'} and were removed at level ℓ', while supp(b) is not contained in Ω_{ℓ̃}. Hence 'T vanishes on Q' does not imply that the level-ℓ̃ representatives of the mother on Q have support in Ω_{ℓ̃}, and the subsequent derivation-containment step is built on an unestablished premise.

issues.failure_explanation: Membership of β_l and β_t in □_{i,j}=□_i∩□_j only gives |l_{k'}-t_{k'}| ≤ 2(p+1) − |j_{k'}−i_{k'}|, which can exceed p+1 when i and j are close in direction k' (e.g. p=1, i=(0,0), j=(1,1) allows |l_{k'}−t_{k'}|=3). Supports (ξ_l,ξ_{l+p+1}) and (ξ_t,ξ_{t+p+1}) then do not intersect (nor touch), so the claimed inclusion supp(β_r) ⊆ closure(supp β_l) ∪ closure(supp β_t) ⊆ Ω_{ℓ+1} for the intermediate β_r fails, and the 'kink removal' step is unjustified. The proof therefore does not establish existence of a shortest chain.

issues.failure_explanation: In Algorithm exact-mesh the variable unchecked_funcs is never initialized: initiate_unchecked_pairs computes it locally but returns only unchecked_pairs. Read literally, after an L-chain is added the new unchecked_pairs = combinations(unchecked_funcs,2) consists only of pairs among corner functions, so a new corner is never tested against pre-existing unresolved B-splines with which it may be problematic. Moreover, enlarging Ω_{ℓ+1} by the L-chain supports can bring further level-ℓ B-splines (whose supports become contained in the enlarged union) into B^0_{ℓ,ℓ+1}; these are neither L-chain members (covered by Lemmas problematic-chain/containment) nor added to unchecked_funcs, so problematic pairs involving them are never checked.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Return unchecked_funcs from initiate_unchecked_pairs, and after each L-chain insertion recompute B^0_{ℓ,ℓ+1}, add all newly entered unresolved B-splines (corners and fill-in functions) to unchecked_funcs, and form new pairs between them and all unresolved functions.
issues.overall_effect: The procedure as written does not guarantee that every pair sharing a minimal (ℓ+1)-intersection is checked, so its output contract ('no problematic intersections') and Lemma added-1 are not ensured.
issues.title: Algorithm exact-mesh: pair-update step is ill-defined and omits pairs involving newly entered B-splines
issues.why_classification: The algorithmic idea survives, but a correct pair-update rule and an accompanying argument covering fill-in functions must be supplied; not a one-line typo.

issues.failure_explanation: Exactness requires (Theorem added-1) that every pair in B^0_{ℓ,ℓ+1} sharing a minimal (ℓ+1)-intersection has a shortest chain, for every ℓ. The one-line proof cites lemmas about L-chains but does not argue that upon termination this hypothesis holds: it does not invoke Theorem added-1 or Lemma containment, does not justify that filtering to non-resolved functions and to pairs touching marked_els is exhaustive, and does not address B-splines entering B through the enlarged Ω_{ℓ+1}. Furthermore, initiate_unchecked_pairs discards all pairs whose supports avoid the marked elements, so the algorithm only certifies pairs affected by the current marking; if the input basis already contains problematic pairs elsewhere they are never repaired, contradicting 'always'.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that the input hierarchical basis is exact (or remove the marked_els filter), and supply a proof that at termination all minimal-intersection pairs at all levels have shortest chains, using Theorem added-1, Lemmas int-box-chain, problematic-sides, problematic-chain and containment, plus a treatment of B-splines that enter B^0_{ℓ,ℓ+1} by fill-in.
issues.overall_effect: The central exactness guarantee of the paper's algorithm is asserted rather than proved, and as stated it is false for inputs that are not already exact.
issues.title: Lemma added-1 ('always produces an exact mesh') is not established by the cited lemmas and overstates the input scope
issues.why_classification: A comparable guarantee (for exact inputs) is recoverable, but a real correctness argument and a hypothesis restriction are needed rather than a local fix.
